text:
Asha (Marketing): quick heads-up — we need a ~30m workshop today to iterate the field-facing claims pack for the next launch + webinar. want tight, testable lines and inbound routing notes. who can join?
Ben (Field): i can. need a single-sheet cheat (objection handlers + 3x soundbites) not a 10-slide deck.
Rohit (Sales): +1. also want two variants for SDRs: one focused on cost control, one on reliability (SLAs/throughput).
Lina (Product): I can pull the latest perf checklist and model-variant table. we should avoid raw latency numbers unless bench team is comfortable. better to use relative claims: "consistent sub-50ms p50 on short seqs"?
Kai (Research): bench-bot just posted fresh numbers for the public models — see link: https://redwood-internal/bench/1766 (shared by bench-bot)
bench-bot: new run 1766 uploaded — 3 models, p50/p95, cost per 1k tokens estimated. digest.csv attached.
Asha (Marketing): perfect. Ben/Rohit — let's craft 3 one-liners for outbound: 1) "Bring predictable latency to LLMs — not just raw speed" 2) "Lower per-token costs without sacrificing quality" 3) "Same API, across hosted, dedicated, and private". thoughts?
Ben (Field): 1 and 3 resonate with platform teams. add a micro-example: "pin a model version & roll out safely" for A/B talk.
Rohit (Sales): for procurement objections, we need short rebuttals: "we offer reserved capacity contracts and enterprise SLAs" and "clear levers to lower unit cost (batching, KV cache, quant profiles) — we can quantify in POC".
Lina (Product): please don't say "quant profiles" to non-technical buyers — maybe "model tuning & quantized runtimes" for field docs. also add a note on security: KMS/HSM + VPC private control plane.
Asha (Marketing): good call. Ben, can you draft the one-pager with 3 soundbites + 5 objection handlers? aim for <300 words. Rohit, can you give 2 SDR email templates (variant cost / variant reliability) — short subject lines too.
Ben (Field): will take this and drop a draft by EOD. rough structure: hero claim, 3 bullets (value props), quick proof (bench bullet), objection handlers, CTA (book POC).
Rohit (Sales): i'll do the SDRs. suggested subjects: "Cut LLM inference costs — quick POC?" and "Shave latency off customer-facing LLM features". i'll A/B them in outbound.
Kai (Research): small nit — call out fallback/graceful degradation as a differentiator vs managed cloud endpoints. many customers care more about uptime during model/region outages than absolute peak perf.
Asha (Marketing): add that under "reliability" bucket. also planning webinar copy: we need a benchmark narrative: not just raw numbers but a story: "how to make inference predictable & cheap at scale" with a short demo: live request routing failover + cost dashboard.
Lina (Product): demo script idea — 8-min walkthrough: 1) cold-start vs cached p50/p95 2) routing rules failover 3) cost/latency dashboard per route. keeps it concrete.
Ben (Field): for field training, give 3 role-play objections: vendor X says "we have faster raw throughput" -> reply: "we trade raw peak for predictable latency per request and built-in failovers — here's a short POC plan".
Rohit (Sales): for inbound tagging — suggest UTMs and SDR routing tags: utm_campaign=llm_ops_launch, tag=cost-POC or tag=reliability-POC. route cost leads to growth SDRs, reliability to enterprise AE queue.
Asha (Marketing): love it. final asks: Ben = one-pager draft by 6pm PT, Rohit = 2 SDR templates by 6pm PT, Kai = confirm bench claims wording (no absolute statements) by 4pm, Lina = demo script & slide outline by EOD. we'll meet 3:30pm for a 25-min review.
Ben (Field): noted. attending 3:30. :thumbsup:
Rohit (Sales): yep. will bring sample outreach cadence.
Lina (Product): on calendar.
Kai (Research): will validate the numbers and post a short blurb for the one-pager.
bench-bot: benchmark run 1766: p50/p95 and est cost uploaded — file: digest_1766.csv
Asha (Marketing): thanks everyone — i'll draft the webinar landing copy after the review and post for quick edits. we should keep language tight and test 2 hero lines in the signup flow.
Ben (Field): quick note for the one-pager: include a tiny diagram showing "same API -> hosted/dedicated/private". visuals help SDRs.
Rohit (Sales): +1. visuals + 2 CTAs (book POC / join webinar).
Asha (Marketing): cool. see you all at 3:30.
